description: Test scenarios for the /qa:automate-functional-tests command. Each eval has expected_behavior assertions with grading methods: file_exists (check file created), grep_pattern (search output for pattern), frontmatter_check (validate YAML frontmatter fields), code_inspection (review generated code for pattern), conversation_check (verify orchestrator behavior in conversation output).

grading_methods.file_exists: Verify the specified file was created in OUTPUT_DIR
grading_methods.grep_pattern: Search generated files for a regex pattern — pass if found (or not found, if negated)
grading_methods.frontmatter_check: Parse YAML frontmatter from a file and validate specific fields
grading_methods.code_inspection: Review generated Java test code for structural patterns (imports, class hierarchy, annotations). REQUIRES A JUDGE — the `pattern` field is a natural-language rubric, not a regex. Grader implementations must route these assertions to a human reviewer or an LLM judge; auto-graders MUST NOT silently pass them. See `benchmarks/iteration-0/README.md` → 'Manual grading burden' for the per-eval count and reviewer-time estimate.
grading_methods.conversation_check: Review orchestrator conversation output for specific messages or decisions

negation_conventions.negated: Boolean flag (true) that FLIPS the polarity of the main `pattern` (or, for file_exists, of the `path` check). Use when the assertion is 'this MUST NOT exist / match'. Example: { grading: 'grep_pattern', pattern: 'import.*quickfixj', negated: true } — passes when the pattern is NOT found.
negation_conventions.negated_pattern: Separate regex string. Adds an AND-combined must-NOT-match constraint alongside the main `pattern` (which must still match). Use when the assertion is 'X must match AND Y must NOT match'. Example: { grading: 'grep_pattern', pattern: 'import.*assertj', negated_pattern: 'import.*junit.*Assert' } — passes when assertj IS found AND junit Assert is NOT found.
negation_conventions.rule: Use `negated: true` for single-constraint must-not assertions. Use `negated_pattern` for two-constraint must-match-X-and-not-Y assertions. The two forms are intentionally distinct — do not unify.

evals.name: small-api-only
evals.description: 3 BE-REST test cases using the concrete sample input file. Should skip Phase 0 entirely, run single-pass Phase 1 (no chunking), compile, review, and fix.

expected_behavior.assertion: Phase 0 skipped (no UI-WEB tests)
expected_behavior.pattern: Phase 0 skip|no UI-WEB|skipping exploration|0 UI.WEB tests

expected_behavior.assertion: Single-pass automation (3 tests < 20 threshold)
Service classes follow zero-defensive-programming pattern
expected_behavior.pattern: no try/catch/if/else/switch in service class methods; methods are 1-3 lines returning ApiResponse

expected_behavior.assertion: All tests use AssertJ assertions
automation-summary.md created
code-review-report.md created with YAML frontmatter
Generated tests deserialize responses via response.as(...) and contain none of the forbidden raw-body / JSON-tree / WebSocket-field patterns
expected_behavior.negated_pattern_intent: Passes only when response.as(...) IS used AND none of these forbidden patterns appear: assertThat(...body()) (any assertion on raw body, not just .contains — uses lazy [\s\S]*? to match multi-line argument expressions and nested calls like assertThat(transform(response.body()))), JsonNode, JsonPath, ObjectMapper.readTree, org.json.* (e.g. JSONObject/JSONArray/JSONTokener), or WebSocketResponse.getField/fields/rawJson. Diagnostic uses (Allure.addAttachment(..., response.body()) / logger.info(..., response.body())) are NOT matched because they don't appear inside assertThat(...).

expected_behavior.assertion: Review report classifies any response.body() / JsonNode / JsonPath / ObjectMapper.readTree / org.json / WebSocketResponse.fields/getField/rawJson usage in assertion context as 🔴 CRITICAL citing the deserialization rule
expected_behavior.pattern: review-report classifies any of the following in assertion context as 🔴 CRITICAL with the deserialization rule cited: response.body() inside assertThat(...), JsonNode, JsonPath, ObjectMapper.readTree, org.json.*, or WebSocketResponse.getField(...)/fields()/rawJson(). Diagnostic raw-body usages in Allure attachments / logger calls should NOT be flagged.

expected_behavior.pattern: at least one *Test.java file created in src/test/java

Max 3 fix attempts enforced — stops and reports if still failing
If compilation succeeds within 3 attempts, proceeds to Phase 2
Compilation status reported to user before Phase 2

Agent MUST keep them as 3 separate @Test methods, NOT combine into a @ParameterizedTest. Tests the parameterization carve-out: 'when each name encodes a semantically distinct scenario, keep tests separate'.

expected_behavior.assertion: Generated tests are 3 separate @Test methods, NOT a single @ParameterizedTest
expected_behavior.pattern: in src/test/java, the three login negative-auth scenarios MUST be implemented as three distinct @Test methods named like test_login_withExpiredToken_returns401, test_login_withRevokedToken_returns401, test_login_withMalformedToken_returns401 (or close equivalents). FAIL if they are combined into a single @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource/@MethodSource/@ValueSource that buries the scenario name in a row.

expected_behavior.assertion: The three token-validation scenarios are not collapsed into a single @ParameterizedTest
expected_behavior.pattern: scoped check — locate the test file(s) implementing the expired-token / revoked-token / malformed-token scenarios (the three TC-FUNC-BE-REST-001/002/003 cases from sample-input-14). PASS if each of the three scenarios is implemented as a separate @Test method in that file. FAIL only if those three scenarios are combined into one @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource/@MethodSource/@ValueSource. Unrelated @ParameterizedTest usages elsewhere in the project (e.g. on other test classes) are out of scope for this assertion and do NOT cause a fail.

expected_behavior.assertion: Review report does NOT flag a MAJOR/CRITICAL issue recommending parameterization for these tests
expected_behavior.pattern: code-review-report.md contains zero CRITICAL or MAJOR issues whose 'description' or 'recommendation' text suggests combining the expired-token / revoked-token / malformed-token tests into a @ParameterizedTest. A MINOR/SUGGESTION note about the carve-out is acceptable.

evals.name: allure-diagnostic-carve-out
evals.description: 2 BE-REST tests that explicitly require raw response.body() inside Allure.addAttachment(...) and logger.info(...) for diagnostics, while still requiring deserialized assertions. Verifies the rule's diagnostic carve-out is respected in both directions: the rule applies to assertions, NOT to diagnostics. Regression check against over-correction.

expected_behavior.assertion: Generated tests deserialize via response.as(...) for the actual assertions
Allure.addAttachment(...) preserves the raw response.body() argument
logger.info / logger.debug / logger.warn preserves the raw response.body() argument
Forbidden raw-body / JSON-tree / org.json patterns DO NOT appear inside assertThat(...)
expected_behavior.negated_pattern_intent: Passes when assertThat(...) IS used AND no forbidden pattern appears inside an assertThat(...) call (uses lazy [\s\S]*? to match multi-line argument expressions). Diagnostic uses outside assertThat(...) are allowed and not matched.

expected_behavior.assertion: Review report does NOT classify the diagnostic Allure / logger raw-body usages as CRITICAL or MAJOR
expected_behavior.pattern: code-review-report.md must NOT contain any CRITICAL or MAJOR issue whose 'description' or 'recommendation' flags the Allure.addAttachment(...) or logger.info(...) raw-body usages. The carve-out is explicitly documented in API_TESTING_GUIDE.yaml → 'Error Response Models'. Flagging these is an over-correction and is itself a review error.

expected_behavior.assertion: automation-summary.md created

evals.name: paginated-envelope-response
evals.description: 2 BE-REST tests where the endpoint returns a wrapped/envelope response (Spring Page<T> shape). Agent MUST declare a wrapper class and use response.as(WrapperClass.class), NOT response.asList(...). Tests the 'list vs envelope' rewrite documented in fix-prompt.md and API_TESTING_GUIDE.yaml → 'Paginated Responses'.

expected_behavior.assertion: Generated tests declare a wrapper class with at least a content field and at least one envelope metadata field (e.g. totalElements / totalPages)
expected_behavior.pattern: in src/main/java (models package), exactly one wrapper class is declared whose shape matches the envelope: at minimum a List-typed `content` field (or getContent() accessor) plus one or more of totalElements, totalPages, size, number. Java records OR classes with getters both acceptable.

expected_behavior.assertion: Generated tests deserialize via response.as(WrapperClass.class) and NOT via response.asList(...)
expected_behavior.negated_pattern_intent: Passes when at least one response.as(WrapperClass.class) call appears AND response.asList(...) is NOT used. The wrapper-class name pattern is permissive (matches *Page*, *Envelope*, or *Response* suffixes) since project naming conventions vary.

expected_behavior.assertion: Tests assert on both the extracted content list AND on envelope metadata (e.g. totalElements)
expected_behavior.pattern: each test asserts on (a) the content list (extracted via page.content() / page.getContent() — typically via assertThat(...).extracting(...) or .hasSize(...)) AND (b) at least one envelope-metadata field (totalElements / totalPages / etc.)

expected_behavior.assertion: No forbidden raw-body / JSON-tree patterns appear in assertion context
expected_behavior.negated_pattern_intent: Same broadened deserialize check as evals 1.7, 13.3, 14.4 — lazy [\s\S]*? for multi-line assertion arguments.

expected_behavior.assertion: automation-summary.md created

evals.name: empty-body-carve-out
evals.description: 2 BE-REST tests where the response has no body by design (204 No Content, 304 Not Modified). Agent MUST assert ONLY on statusCode() and NOT call response.as(...) on the empty body. Tests the empty-body carve-out documented in API_TESTING_GUIDE.yaml → 'Error Response Models'.

expected_behavior.assertion: Generated tests assert on statusCode() for the 204/304 responses
Generated tests do NOT call response.as(...) on the 204 or 304 responses
expected_behavior.pattern: in src/test/java, for the test methods asserting HTTP 204 (delete-order) and HTTP 304 (conditional-get not-modified), there must be NO response.as(...) call on the SAME ApiResponse variable that holds the 204/304 result. Other tests in the file may still use response.as(...) on their own 2xx responses — that is fine. FAIL only if the agent attempted to deserialize the empty body.

expected_behavior.assertion: Generated tests do NOT call response.body() in assertion context for 204/304 responses
expected_behavior.negated_pattern_intent: Passes when status-code assertions ARE present AND no assertThat(...body()) appears anywhere — the empty-body carve-out forbids body assertions, and these two tests have no other 2xx responses with bodies that would legitimately need .body() in assertion context (the 200 ETag-capture step is a SETUP, not an assertion target). Lazy [\s\S]*? handles multi-line assertion arguments.

expected_behavior.assertion: Header assertions via response.raw().headers() ARE allowed and may appear
expected_behavior.pattern: if the agent asserts on response headers (e.g. ETag, Location) it must go through response.raw().headers().firstValue(...) — never through response.body() or response.as(...). This assertion PASSES whether or not header assertions are present; it only FAILS if header assertions are present BUT use the wrong API.

expected_behavior.assertion: automation-summary.md created

evals.name: header-assertion-carve-out
evals.description: 2 BE-REST tests where the verification target is an HTTP response header (Location after POST 201, Retry-After on 503). Agent MUST use response.raw().headers().firstValue(...) — never response.body() or response.as(...) for header access. Tests the header-check carve-out documented in API_TESTING_GUIDE.yaml → 'Error Response Models' in isolation (eval 18 brushes it as an 'if-present' check only).

expected_behavior.assertion: Phase 0 skipped (no UI-WEB tests)
expected_behavior.pattern: Phase 0 skip|no UI-WEB|skipping exploration|0 UI.WEB tests

expected_behavior.assertion: Header assertions use response.raw().headers().firstValue(...)
Header assertions cover both the Location (201) and Retry-After (503) targets
expected_behavior.pattern: the test method asserting HTTP 201 verifies the Location header via response.raw().headers().firstValue("Location"); the test method asserting HTTP 503 verifies Retry-After via response.raw().headers().firstValue("Retry-After"). Both must be present.

expected_behavior.assertion: Body deserialization still applies for the 201 success path (typed assertion on the body in addition to the header)
No forbidden raw-body / JSON-tree patterns appear in assertion context
expected_behavior.negated_pattern_intent: Passes when the header-access API IS used AND no raw-body / JSON-tree pattern appears in an assertion. Header access via raw().headers() is the explicit carve-out — body() and JSON-tree parsing are still forbidden in assertion context.

expected_behavior.assertion: Review report does NOT flag the response.raw().headers() usage as CRITICAL or MAJOR
expected_behavior.pattern: code-review-report.md must NOT contain any CRITICAL or MAJOR issue whose 'description' or 'recommendation' flags the response.raw().headers().firstValue(...) header-assertion API. The header carve-out is documented in API_TESTING_GUIDE.yaml → 'Error Response Models' as explicitly allowed. Flagging it is an over-correction and is itself a review error.
